title: Bytes heuristics next_layer inspects (QUIC, host header, raw TCP)
answers: When is traffic treated as raw TCP?
How is the HTTP Host header sniffed?
body:
In `mitmproxy/addons/next_layer.py`:
- `_starts_like_quic`: False if <18 bytes or looks like DTLS; long-header packet -> True if version in `KNOWN_QUIC_VERSIONS` or matches reserved `0x?a?a?a?a`; else fallback to server port in `TYPICAL_QUIC_PORTS` (80, 443, 8443).
- `_get_host_header`: TCP only, no server data yet; needs request line matching `[A-Z]{3,}.+HTTP/`, finds `Host:` before blank line; raises `NeedsMoreData` until headers complete.
- `_get_client_hello`: TCP `parse_client_hello`; UDP `quic_parse_client_hello_from_datagrams` then `dtls_parse_client_hello`. Incomplete -> NeedsMoreData; parse failure -> no hello.
- `probably_no_http` (only used when `--rawtcp`): true if <3 bytes, no space, first space after first newline, first 3 bytes non-alpha, server sent first, or data starts with `SSH`.
